rules.localIntel: Hand-curated from primary sources: each item was read at its own source on the date shown, states only what that source says, and quotes it where a quote is given. Where a source does not settle something (a winner, an end date) the item says not verified. Every link is re-checked on each daily build; an item whose source has gone is withdrawn until it is re-sourced. This is not a census: it lists the contracts, formularies and papers found and read, not every one that exists.
rules.frameworks: NHS Supply Chain framework names matching /\b(respiratory solutions|non invasive ventilation|airway management|anaesthesia machines)\b/i. NHSSC names a framework after its clinical category, so the name is the key; the CBU category field is far too broad to filter on. COVERAGE LIMITS, STATED RATHER THAN HIDDEN. Two of the four agreements above are shared routes rather than respiratory ones: Airway Management Products is categorised by NHS Supply Chain under Medical and Surgical Consumables and is claimed by theatres and surgical, and Anaesthesia Machines, Ventilators, Neonatal Equipment and Phototherapy Systems is claimed by theatres and surgical and by maternity and neonatal, with this page claiming only the ventilator half. Being named on a framework is not evidence of volume on this patch, and being absent from one is not evidence of absence from the market. The supplier list is built from the four frameworks, so it counts airway and anaesthesia houses alongside respiratory ones; overlap is the better guide to who is really on this patch. In the list below, suppliers on all four frameworks: 1; on three: 5. Home oxygen is the largest gap and it is a real one: it is bought through regional Home Oxygen Service contracts, not through any national NHS Supply Chain framework, so it appears in awards and tenders and nowhere else. The community medicines half of this patch — the larger half by money — is FP10 prescribing under BNF Chapter 3 and has no framework and no Drug Tariff Part IX presence at all.

rules.awards: Award-stage notices whose TITLE matches /\b(respirator\w*|pulmonary function\w*|pulmonary diagnostic\w*|pulmonary rehabilitation|lung function|lung volume|asthma|copd|chronic obstructive pulmonary|bronchoscop\w*|bronchodilat\w*|bronchiectasis|spirometr\w*|spirometer\w*|peak flow|feno|fractional exhaled nitric oxide|nitric oxide|oxygen|nebulis\w*|nebuliz\w*|inhaler\w*|ventilator\w*|(?:non-?invasive|mechanical|home|nasal|neonatal|infant|patient|jet|transport|critical care) ventilation|cpap|bipap|continuous positive airway pressure|sleep (?:apnoea|apnea|therapy|monitoring|diagnostic\w*|stud\w*)|apnoea|apnea|polysomnograph\w*|airway\w*|intubat\w*|laryngoscop\w*|tracheostom\w*|tracheotom\w*|tracheal|endotracheal|breathing circuit\w*|breathing system\w*|cystic fibrosis|pleural|chest drain\w*|pneumothorax|pneumonia|cough assist|high[- ]flow nasal)\b/i and does not match /\b(hyperbaric|epoc devices?|newborn screening)\b/i. The exclusion list exists because every pattern in it matched a real notice that was not this speciality. A CPV code beginning 33157 is recorded as corroboration where the feed carries one, but never admits a notice on its own: a notice carrying a basket of CPV codes is filed under all of them and bought under one. Buyer names are never matched on.
rules.openTenders: Notices still open for bidding, matched the same way. An empty list means no open notice on this patch today, not that none was looked for.
rules.drugTariff: NHSBSA Drug Tariff Part IXA for the stated effective month, narrowed to the lines whose virtual medicinal product description matches /peak flow meter|tracheostomy (?:breathing aid|tube holder|cleaning device)|tracheostomy and laryngectomy protector/i, and then summarised. The part is sliced rather than claimed whole because the part is not this speciality: Part IXA is 56,879 lines of dressings and elastic hosiery, which are the tissue viability page's, and only the lines this pattern selects belong here. Every count and price below is taken from those lines. Prices are the reimbursement price at publication, converted from the pence NHSBSA publishes, and are not necessarily today's.
rules.directorySuppliers: Companies the Hub's own supplier directory files under this speciality, from the speciality labels on each company's directory record, resolved through speciality-label-map.json and speciality-map.json (Compare ids: respiratory). They are labelled DIRECTORY-TAGGED because the tag is the Hub's filing of a company's range, not a procurement record: being listed here is not evidence of a contract or of volume, and the list is not a census of the market. A company that is also on this speciality's own frameworks is listed once, with the framework-named suppliers, and marked as also directory-tagged. WHERE A COMPANY IS ON ANOTHER FRAMEWORK: where a directory-tagged company is named on an NHS Supply Chain framework that is not counted as this speciality's, it is still listed, with that framework named against it and linked, so it is not lost from the page. 11 of the 12 listed here carry such a note. Framework names and links come from NHS Supply Chain's own contract launch briefs as held in frameworks.json; an agreement the directory records from another buying organisation, such as an NHS Shared Business Services framework, is shown as the directory states it.
rules.gpPrescribing: Items prescribed in primary care in England (GP practices and other prescribers NHSBSA attributes to a practice) and dispensed in the community, aggregated to ICB. Not hospital in-patient use, and not the trust-level hospital prescribing dataset. Source: NHSBSA Open Data: English Prescribing Dataset (EPD) with SNOMED code. Each market below is a set of BNF codes exactly as NHSBSA classifies them, named with the market. Figures are for the latest month in the dataset (202607) with a 12-month total; a change on the same month a year earlier is published only where that month had at least 25 items, and otherwise no percentage is printed. Share is share of ITEMS by NHSBSA product (BNF code characters 1 to 11, split to 13 where a catch-all code holds several brands). It is product share, not company share: the dataset does not name the company, and one company can hold several products. An ICB's leaders are ranked within that ICB's own total for the same market and month. Contains public sector information licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0. Source: NHS Business Services Authority.
rules.mhraDsu: Every MHRA Drug Safety Update that GOV.UK itself tags to a therapeutic area mapped to this speciality in config/mhra-dsu-speciality-map.json. The speciality comes only from GOV.UK's own facet, never from the title or the text. The monthly 'Letters and medicine recalls sent to healthcare professionals' roundup is left out (16 here), and so is any update GOV.UK ticks against 30 or more therapeutic areas, which is a message to everyone rather than to this speciality (2 here). Newest first; the count is every tagged update in the archive, and the list shows the most recent. MHRA Drug Safety Update, GOV.UK, as at 2026-10-05.
rules.drugTariffViiia: NHSBSA Drug Tariff Part VIIIA, the basic prices of generic medicines, for effective month 2026-10: narrowed to the lines whose medicine NHSBSA prescribes under BNF chapter 3. The BNF code is the one NHSBSA attaches to the line's VMP SNOMED code in its English Prescribing Dataset, the same classification-first approach as the Part IX slice, never a medicine-name pattern. 53 of the 3,534 lines in the file carry no BNF code because the medicine was not prescribed in primary care in the months read, so this slice can understate the range and does not overstate it. Every count and price is taken from the lines selected. Prices are the basic price at publication, converted from the pence NHSBSA publishes, and are not necessarily today's. The list shows at most 80 lines, Category M first.

updates.title: Nasal decongestant sprays and drops containing xylometazoline hydrochloride / oxymetazoline hydrochloride: increased risk of rebound congestion, rhinitis medicamentosa, and tachyphylaxis with overuse
updates.summary: There have been reports of worsening nasal congestion (rebound congestion) when the effects of nasal decongestant sprays or drops containing xylometazoline hydrochloride and oxymetazoline hydrochloride, wear off.

updates.title: Abrysvo▼ (Pfizer RSV vaccine) and Arexvy▼ (GSK RSV vaccine): be alert to a small risk of Guillain-Barré syndrome following vaccination in older adults
updates.summary: There is a small increase in the risk of Guillain-Barré syndrome following vaccination with Abrysvo (Pfizer respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) vaccine) and Arexvy (GSK RSV vaccine) in adults aged 60 years and older. Healthcare professionals should advise all recipients of Abrysvo and Arexvy that they should be alert to signs and symptoms of Guillain-Barré syndrome and, if they occur, to seek immediate medical attention as it requires urgent treatment in hospital.

updates.title: Kaftrio▼ (Ivacaftor, tezacaftor, elexacaftor): risk of psychological side effects
updates.summary: Psychological side effects such as anxiety, low mood, sleep disturbance, poor concentration, and forgetfulness have been infrequently reported in people with cystic fibrosis treated with Kaftrio. Healthcare professionals should advise patients and their caregivers that, while the risk is small, they should be alert to changes in mood and behaviour and, if they occur, to seek medical advice as soon as possible.

updates.title: Short-acting beta 2 agonists (SABA) (salbutamol and terbutaline): reminder of the risks from overuse in asthma and to be aware of changes in the SABA prescribing guidelines
updates.summary: Healthcare professionals and patients are reminded of the risk of severe asthma attacks and increased mortality associated with overuse of SABA with or without anti-inflammatory maintenance therapy in patients with asthma. Healthcare professionals should be aware of the change in guidance that no longer recommends prescribing SABA without an inhaled corticosteroid.

updates.title: Montelukast: reminder of the risk of neuropsychiatric reactions
updates.summary: Healthcare professionals prescribing montelukast should be alert to the risk of neuropsychiatric reactions in all patients including children and adolescents. Reported neuropsychiatric reactions include sleep disorders, hallucinations, anxiety and depression, as well as changes in behaviour and mood. Healthcare professionals should advise patients and their caregivers to be alert to these risks and seek medical advice as soon as possible if neuropsychiatric reactions occur.

updates.title: Pseudoephedrine: very rare risk of posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome (PRES) and reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome (RCVS)
updates.summary: There have been very rare reports of posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome (PRES) and reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome (RCVS) with pseudoephedrine.

updates.title: Codeine linctus (codeine oral solutions): reclassification to prescription-only medicine
updates.summary: Advice for healthcare professionals on the reclassification of codeine linctus to a prescription-only medicine (POM), following a public consultation.

updates.title: Nirmatrelvir, ritonavir (Paxlovid▼): be alert to the risk of drug interactions with ritonavir
updates.summary: There is a risk of harmful drug interactions with the ritonavir component of the COVID-19 treatment Paxlovid▼ due to its inhibition of the enzyme CYP3A, which metabolises many commonly used drugs. Prescribers should obtain a detailed patient history of current medications before prescribing Paxlovid, checking the Paxlovid product information for known and potential drug interactions.
